attributes.residual: ONE net instruction plus a callee-saved allocation gap, fully localised. The target saves FOUR callee-saved registers (`stmw r28,112(r1)`) and we save THREE (`stmw r29,116(r1)`) in an identical 128-byte frame. The target's extra instruction is `addi r30,r31,0` at +0x28: it computes the player pointer into r31, immediately COPIES it to r30, uses r31 through the cheat block, then RECYCLES r31 as the zero constant (`li r31,0` at +0x118). Our build never makes that copy, keeps p in r31 throughout, and puts zero in r29. Register roles are a 3-cycle plus one extra: ours zero=r29,i=r30,p=r31 against target i=r29,p=r30,zero=r31, with the target additionally holding lvl in r28 across the set_player_default_atts/check_player_atts calls (`stw r28,13092(r31)` at +0xcc) where ours reuses r29 for lvl-then-zero. Through the whole cheat block (+0x60 to +0xd4) the two streams are structurally IDENTICAL and differ only in register names. NEXT LANE'S MANDATORY STEP 1 (untried hypothesis, per discipline 10b): force a fourth callee-saved live value so `lvl` gets its own register and p can be pre-copied - the declaration/initializer-order lever of claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1 applied to `lvl`/`exp`/`product`, which was screened but NOT probed this session.
